title: Fix a Security Group That Exposes SSH to the Internet
intro: A security scan flagged this Terraform: the web servers' security group allows SSH from anywhere. The team now uses SSM Session Manager for shell access (aws-tutorial-003), so SSH doesn't need to be open at all.

steps.prompt:
Edit sg.tf:
(1) Remove the SSH ingress block entirely.
(2) Keep HTTPS (443) ingress from 0.0.0.0/0, and give it a description = "HTTPS from the internet".
(3) Add a description = "Web servers: HTTPS only, shell access via SSM" to the security group itself.
(4) Keep the egress block.

fields.resource.aws_security_group.web.descript: Web servers: HTTPS only, shell access via SSM

steps.hint: Delete the whole first ingress { ... } block (the one with from_port = 22). Add description = "..." inside the remaining ingress block and at the top of the resource.
steps.explanation: SSH is no longer reachable from anywhere; HTTPS is unchanged. The plan is an in-place update (no downtime), and the scanner is clean.
steps.why: The best firewall rule is the one you don't need. With SSM Session Manager, admins get shells through IAM-authorised, logged sessions and port 22 can be closed entirely, which removes brute-force risk (security-incident-001) and key sprawl in one move. Descriptions aren't decoration: during an audit or incident, 'why does this rule exist?' should be answered by the rule itself. One gotcha: changing a security group's description forces Terraform to replace the group. Here that happens in the same apply, but on a live group, check the plan for '-/+' before applying.
